questions.question: The passage focusses on the problem of
questions.questionHtml: The passage focusses on the problem of
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'malnutrition'. 

Key Points

  • The given passage is about 'Malnutrition'. 
  • Modern-day India represents a paradoxical situation where a large section of society (the poorest two-fifths of the country’s population) is still largely untouched by the modern economy which the rest of the country inhabits.
  • Despite rapid economic growth, declining levels of poverty, enough food to export, and a multiplicity of government programs, malnutrition amongst the poorest in India remains high.
  • Malnutrition is a condition that results from eating a diet that does not supply a healthy amount of one or more nutrients.
  • This includes diets that have too little nutrients or so many that the diet causes health problems.  
  • The passage tells us that the setting up of the National Nutrition Council and Integrated Child Development Scheme is not of much help. 
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is Option 3. 
    ​

Correct Answer: malnutrition.

questions.question: What is the ANTONYM of the word ‘perfect’, as used in the passage?

questions.solution:

Key Points

  • Perfect: (उत्तम) - Having all the required or desirable elements, qualities, or characteristics; as good as it is possible to be.

  • Unsatisfactory: (असंतोषजनक) - Not satisfactory; not good enough.

  • Laughable: (हास्यास्पद) - So ludicrous as to be amusing.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate title for the passage.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate title for the passage.

options.text: Development of Fine Motor Skills in Children
options.html: Development of Fine Motor Skills in Children

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Development of Fine Motor Skills in Children'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage extensively discusses the various stages and milestones of fine motor skill development in children.
  • It details how children evolve in their capabilities, starting from a reflexive grip at birth to being able to handle crayons and cut with scissors as toddlers.
  • The focus is specifically on the abilities that involve small muscles in the hands, fingers, and thumbs, demonstrating tasks like writing, feeding themselves, and dressing.
  • Every developmental milestone mentioned relates directly to the improvement of fine motor skills over time, making this title the most encapsulating for the content provided.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.
 
Additional Information
  • Importance of Fine Motor Skills: This option, while relevant, is too generic and does not capture the specific focus on the development and stages of these skills as outlined in the passage.
  • Systematic Development of Children: This title might seem applicable, but it’s too broad. The passage does not discuss the overall systematic development of children but specifically focuses on the aspect of fine motor skills.
  • Development of New-borns: This title is misleading as it suggests the passage deals only with the initial stages of life. In contrast, the passage covers fine motor skills development from birth up to the age of four, making this option too narrow.

questions.question: In light of the above passage, which of the following toys may help in the development of fine motor skills?
questions.questionHtml: In light of the above passage, which of the following toys may help in the development of fine motor skills?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'All of the given options'.
 
Key Points
  • The passage mentions various activities and tools that contribute to the development of fine motor skills in children, which include handling crayons, stringing beads, and stacking building blocks.
  • Crayons are mentioned as being used by toddlers to paint and draw with their thumb and fingers instead of their fist, which aids in fine motor skills development.
  • String beads are highlighted as an activity for two-year-olds to help with their fine motor skills, involving the use of their thumb and fingers in a precise manner.
  • Stacking building blocks is described as an activity of interest for children between the ages of 12 and 24 months, which assists in the development of fine motor skills by requiring balance, coordination, and precision.
  • Since all these toys are directly mentioned in the context of developing fine motor skills, they all contribute to this aspect of a child's development.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 2'.
 
Additional Information
  • Crayons: Help in developing grip and drawing skills, mentioned for toddlers to enhance motor control and creativity.
  • String beads: Improve precision and dexterity as children use their fingers to manipulate small objects.
  • Stacks and building blocks: Encourage problem-solving and hand-eye coordination, as children learn to balance and arrange objects.
  • Each option is individually mentioned in the passage as beneficial for developing fine motor skills, highlighting why collectively, they all are suitable choices.

questions.question: When do children learn to regulate the release of the objects that they are gripping?
questions.questionHtml: When do children learn to regulate the release of the objects that they are gripping?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '6 - 12 months'.
 
Key Points
  • The development of fine motor skills encompasses various stages, including the ability to regulate the release of objects.
  • During the 6 to 12 months age interval, babies transition from reflexive grasping to more intentional actions with their hands and fingers.
  • This period is characterized by infants developing the capability to not only grab objects but also to release them deliberately, which is a crucial step in fine motor development.
  • It signifies the beginning of more precise and controlled use of the fingers and hands, setting the foundation for more complex tasks like feeding themselves, drawing, and playing with smaller toys.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
 
Additional Information
  • 3 - 6 months: At this stage, infants are primarily developing their grasp reflex and might start to reach for and hold objects, but the regulation of release is not yet refined.
  • 2 - 4 years: This is a period where children have already developed the basic fine motor skills and are refining their abilities, such as drawing and cutting with scissors, which is beyond the skill of regulating object release.
  • 12 - 24 months: Children in this age group are enhancing their fine motor skills further, engaging in more complex activities than simply releasing objects, such as stacking blocks accurately or stringing beads.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Systematically
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Systematically
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Haphazardly'.
 
Key Points
  • The word "systematically" refers to doing something in a systematic order or methodical way, where there is a clear plan or system in place (सुव्यवस्थित तरीके से).
    • Example: The librarian organized the books systematically by genre and then by author’s last name.
  • The antonym "haphazardly" means to do something in a manner lacking any obvious principle of organization, or in a random, chaotic way (यदाकदा).
    • Example: Clothes were thrown haphazardly around the room without any order.
  • Hence, the correct antonym is Haphazardly.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 4'.
 
Additional Information
  • Evenly: This word means in a smooth and steady manner (समान रूप से). It doesn't fit as an antonym to systematically because both suggest a form of organization or balance.
    • Example: The paint needs to be applied evenly to ensure a smooth finish.
  • Selectively: This means to choose something with care or discernment (चयनात्मक रूप से). While it involves making choices, it doesn’t inherently contrast with doing something systematically.
    • Example: She goes through her emails selectively, responding first to the most urgent.
  • Oddly: This is used to indicate that something is strange or unusual (अजीब तरह से). It does not serve as a direct antonym to systematically since it’s more about the quality of strangeness than about the method or organization.
    • Example: Oddly enough, he felt calm in the midst of chaos.

questions.question: When do children get interested in playing with building blocks?
questions.questionHtml: When do children get interested in playing with building blocks?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '12 - 24 months'.
 
Key Points
  • According to the details provided in the context of fine motor skill development, children start showing an interest in playing with building blocks between the ages of 12 to 24 months.
  • This stage of development marks when children are enhancing their hand-eye coordination and beginning to explore objects in their environment with more intention.
  • Playing with building blocks requires some level of motor skill that children in this age group are developing, such as the ability to grasp, stack, and balance objects, which aligns with their developmental milestones around this time.
Therefore, the correct answer is 'Option 1'.
 
Additional Information
  • 0 - 6 months: Infants at this stage are mostly focused on developing basic motor skills and sensory experiences. They are likely too young to show a specific interest in playing with building blocks.
  • 6 - 12 months: While babies in this age group start to grasp and manipulate objects, their ability to purposefully stack or build with blocks is still developing and not as refined as it is from 12-24 months.
  • 2 - 4 years: Children in this age range certainly enjoy playing with building blocks, but the specific interest and developmentally appropriate stage for starting to engage with building blocks as mentioned aligns with the 12 - 24 months period.
